task: Implement the accepted plan Story 1 as additive contract and measurement infrastructure while preserving all 16 current role Prompt outputs byte-for-byte.
outcome: Running lattice prompt_measurement_report prints roleCount=16, explicit active/compatibility/retired counts, deterministic bytes/lines/estimated-token/repetition metrics, and known/provider input layers as unavailable where they are not observable; the baseline verifier still reports all 16 agent_prompt output hashes unchanged.
facts: packages/main/src/core/prompt-registry.ts is the package-owned source for exactly 16 prompt template bodies and agent_prompt returns those bodies byte-for-byte.
docs/requirements/baselines/proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.json plus scripts/verify-proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.mjs already freeze all 16 output hashes and bytes.

AGENT_DISPATCH_REGISTRY already canonicalizes test-intent and test-case-reviewer to verification-intent and keeps product-reviewer as an INIT reviewer, but it is a dispatch authority table rather than a lifecycle status contract.

The verifier-only ROLE_MATRIX_DEFAULTS currently uses legacy status vocabulary that conflicts with the accepted plan for product-reviewer, implementation-reviewer, test-intent, and test-case-reviewer.
LOAD_BEARING_LATTICE_PROMPT_SLICE is already byte-identical inside active prompt bodies and can seed the additive RuntimeContract without changing assembled output.
The usage-ledger bytesCharsEstimator already pins an offline UTF-8 bytes/4 estimator at version 1 and should be reused rather than duplicated.
constraints: Do not alter agent_prompt output, current dispatch routing, reviewer gates, or ReviewRun signatures in Story 1.
PromptMeasurementRecord is the only produced baseline record; PromptEnvelope is a validated schema only and must not be instantiated or persisted.
Unknown known-dispatch/provider input must be represented as unavailable with a reason, never zero.
New CLI semantics must be registered in command policy, process fact registry, all-phase/read-only routing, and mechanical verifiers.
Canonical serialization, line counting, token estimation, path ordering, and repetition algorithms must have explicit versions and deterministic mutation tests.
